release_summary.summary:
The requester (SH-CS) asked for an AI agent to auto-answer tickets and auto-fix wrong bills (CL-01), implying a response-speed/automation gap (H-AUTOMATION-GAP). That hypothesis was REJECTED: CRM response times are within SLA (E-03). The established root problem (PD-1) is instead a billing import/validation rule defect: dispute tickets roughly doubled (E-07); 59% of disputed bills carry an ACTUAL read type (E-01), ruling out simple estimate-substitution; no tariff change was logged (E-02); and most disputed ESTIMATED-read bills (1184/1240, E-12) had valid AMI reads rejected on import for high consumption, unifying both disputed-bill groups under one likely cause (H-RULE-CHANGE). A field route-completion shortfall (E-04) and SH-FIELD's staffing claim (E-06) are treated only as an assumed secondary contributor, not the primary driver.

The DEFINE Gate reached CONDITIONAL_PASS, deferring some confirmation work as verification obligations (VOBs). The release decision is RELEASE_WITH_KNOWN_LIMITATION, nothing on hold. Released scope covers read-only analysis/monitoring (disputed-bill analysis, route-completion cross-reference, dispute-volume/response-time trend monitoring); the route-priority-update capability remains blocked pending SH-FIELD runtime confirmation and open VOB-R-2 about the staffing claim's credibility. No automated bill write occurs; bill correction stays a manual, Billing-Operations-approved action.

The release carries known limitations, including two internal-consistency problems the verifier flagged: the limitation text claims the VOB blocking SC-1 and the field-contribution unknown are still open, while the underlying state records both as RESOLVED. This mismatch is reported, not silently corrected, alongside other unresolved items (unverified staffing claim, unknown tool health, unknown field-to-billing handoff status).

output.summary:
The requester (SH-CS) asked for an AI agent to auto-answer tickets and auto-fix wrong bills (CL-01), implying a response-speed/automation gap (H-AUTOMATION-GAP). That hypothesis was REJECTED: CRM response times are within SLA (E-03). The established root problem (PD-1) is instead a billing import/validation rule defect: dispute tickets roughly doubled (E-07); 59% of disputed bills carry an ACTUAL read type (E-01), ruling out simple estimate-substitution; no tariff change was logged (E-02); and most disputed ESTIMATED-read bills (1184/1240, E-12) had valid AMI reads rejected on import for high consumption, unifying both disputed-bill groups under one likely cause (H-RULE-CHANGE). A field route-completion shortfall (E-04) and SH-FIELD's staffing claim (E-06) are treated only as an assumed secondary contributor, not the primary driver.

The DEFINE Gate reached CONDITIONAL_PASS, deferring some confirmation work as verification obligations (VOBs). The release decision is RELEASE_WITH_KNOWN_LIMITATION, nothing on hold. Released scope covers read-only analysis/monitoring (disputed-bill analysis, route-completion cross-reference, dispute-volume/response-time trend monitoring); the route-priority-update capability remains blocked pending SH-FIELD runtime confirmation and open VOB-R-2 about the staffing claim's credibility. No automated bill write occurs; bill correction stays a manual, Billing-Operations-approved action.

The release carries known limitations, including two internal-consistency problems the verifier flagged: the limitation text claims the VOB blocking SC-1 and the field-contribution unknown are still open, while the underlying state records both as RESOLVED. This mismatch is reported, not silently corrected, alongside other unresolved items (unverified staffing claim, unknown tool health, unknown field-to-billing handoff status).
